astronomy.label: Shared astronomical measurements
astronomy.phaseLabelMethod: Eight broad 45° ecliptic-elongation sectors, not an exact phase-event search
limitations: Geocentric positions; not a camera observation. Julian day uses uniform UTC-like days, without a separate leap-second or TT conversion.

calculationLimitations: Computed sky positions and civil dates are distinct from traditional symbolic interpretations. Astrology has no demonstrated predictive validity.
Calendar rows use the selected zone’s civil midnight. Hebrew and Islamic religious days can begin at sunset; this comparison does not calculate their ritual-day dates or observances.
A shared solar or lunar input is mathematical dependence, not independent agreement or evidence that traditions predict the same outcome.
Complete comparison is bounded to UTC years 1900–2100, matching existing civil-calendar and prayer engines. Time-zone and non-Gregorian displays depend on runtime Intl/ICU data.
Coordinates do not determine an IANA zone. The caller must check that the supplied location and civil zone belong together.
Favorable, caution and neutral describe named traditional rule classes for the sampled instant, not a prediction, personal judgment, or a verdict on the entire civil day.
Optional actions are modern editorial reflection exercises. They are not quotations from a historical book or required activities.
Separate testimonies can disagree; there is no universal score, vote, confidence percentage, or cancellation of cautions by favorable rules.
Civil-calendar date names do not imply good or bad days. Religious observances, personal birth data, fixed-star positions, and horary questions are not inferred.

The selected subset omits the legacy aggregate chart-health score, question-specific early/late Ascendant and radicality rules, void-of-course approximations, house-based judgments, and unprecessed historical fixed-star tables.
